title: Review: Electron configurations

Terms and clues: S1.3#c03 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; S1.3#c19 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S1.3#c18 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S1.3#c01 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Photon
items.clue: A discrete packet (quantum) of electromagnetic radiation.

items.label: Aufbau principle
items.clue: In the ground state, the lowest-energy orbitals are occupied first.

items.label: Hund’s rule
items.clue: Electrons fill orbitals of equal energy singly before any pairing occurs.

items.label: Emission spectrum
items.clue: The pattern of electromagnetic radiation given out by a substance, spread out by wavelength (for example by a prism or diffraction grating).

questions.stem: When sodium compounds are heated in a flame, the flame turns yellow. Which process in the sodium atoms produces this yellow light?

options.text: Excited electrons fall to lower energy levels, emitting photons.
Electrons absorb energy and emit photons as they rise to higher levels.
Electrons escape from the atoms entirely, releasing energy as photons.
The hot atoms glow with the yellow colour that sodium atoms possess.

questions.explanation: Heat excites electrons to higher energy levels. When they fall back to lower levels, each transition emits a photon whose energy equals the difference between the two levels; the main sodium transitions give yellow light.

questions.stem: In the hydrogen emission spectrum, transitions ending at n = 1 produce lines in the ultraviolet region. In which region are the lines produced by transitions ending at n = 3, and why?

options.text: Infrared, because the energy gaps from higher levels down to n = 3 are smaller than those down to n = 2
Ultraviolet, because n = 3 is a higher energy level than n = 2, so its photons carry more energy
Ultraviolet, because the levels above n = 3 are more widely spaced than the levels above n = 2
Visible, because the levels are equally spaced, so every fall releases the same size of energy step

questions.stem: What is the maximum total number of electrons that the first three main energy levels of an atom (n = 1, 2 and 3) can hold?
questions.explanation: Level n holds a maximum of 2n² electrons: 2 × 1² = 2, 2 × 2² = 8 and 2 × 3² = 18, giving 2 + 8 + 18 = 28.

questions.stem: Which description of the shapes and orientations of the three 2p atomic orbitals is correct?

options.text: Three dumbbell shapes along the x, y and z axes, at 90° to one another
Three dumbbell shapes lying in one plane, at 120° to one another
Three figure-of-eight paths that the electrons follow around the nucleus
A single dumbbell shape that holds all six electrons of the 2p sublevel

questions.explanation: Each p orbital is a dumbbell with two lobes on opposite sides of the nucleus. The three p orbitals of a sublevel point along the three perpendicular axes: px, py and pz.

questions.stem: Which full electron configuration of a ground-state atom is correct?

options.text: scandium: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 4p¹
cobalt: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁹
iron: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶ 4s²
germanium: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹² 4s²

questions.explanation: Iron (Z = 26) has 26 electrons. Filling in the order 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d gives 18 electrons up to 3p⁶, then 4s², then the remaining six in 3d: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶ 4s² ([Ar] 3d⁶ 4s²).

questions.stem: White light from a hot filament lamp gives a continuous spectrum when it is passed through a prism. Light from a hydrogen discharge tube passed through the same prism gives a line spectrum. How does the line spectrum differ from the continuous spectrum?

options.text: It shows dark lines at certain wavelengths, across a continuous band of colour.
It shows only one bright line, since a hydrogen atom has only one electron.
It shows bright lines at only certain wavelengths, on a dark background.
It shows bright lines at frequencies spaced at equal intervals across it.

questions.explanation: A continuous spectrum contains every wavelength over a range. The hydrogen atoms emit only photons of certain energies, so the line emission spectrum consists of separate bright lines at particular wavelengths with darkness between them.

questions.stem: Which electron transition in a hydrogen atom emits the photon of highest frequency?
questions.explanation: Photon energy, and therefore frequency, equals the energy difference between the two levels. Falls to n = 1 involve the largest gaps, because the levels are much further apart near n = 1. The n = 4 → n = 1 fall releases far more energy than 6 → 2 or 6 → 5.

questions.stem: A potassium atom (Z = 19) has the electron arrangement 2, 8, 8, 1: two electrons in the first main energy level, eight in the second, eight in the third and one in the fourth. Which statement about the third main energy level (n = 3) of this atom is correct?

options.text: It is not full, because a level with n = 3 can hold up to 2 × 3² = 18 electrons.
It is full, because every main energy level after the first holds a maximum of 8 electrons.
It is full, because electrons only enter the fourth level once the third holds all it can.
It is not full, because it has n² = 9 orbitals and so has room for one more electron.

questions.stem: In a potassium atom, the nineteenth electron occupies the 4s sublevel rather than the 3d sublevel. What is the reason?

options.text: The 4s orbital is nearer the nucleus, and orbitals fill from the inside outward.
Hund’s rule requires an s sublevel to be filled before any d sublevel.
The third main energy level is already full, as it holds at most eight electrons.
The 4s sublevel is lower in energy than the 3d sublevel in this atom.

questions.explanation: Electrons occupy the lowest-energy orbitals available (the Aufbau principle). In potassium and calcium, the 4s sublevel is lower in energy than 3d, so it fills first: potassium is [Ar] 4s¹.

questions.stem: An iron atom (Z = 26) has the condensed electron configuration [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². How is an Fe²⁺ ion formed from this atom?

options.text: Two of the six 3d electrons are removed from the atom.
One 4s electron and one 3d electron are each removed.
Two electrons are added to the 3d sublevel of the atom.
Both of the 4s electrons are removed from the atom.

questions.explanation: When a transition element forms a positive ion, the 4s electrons are removed before the 3d electrons. Removing both 4s electrons from [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s² gives Fe²⁺, [Ar] 3d⁶, with 24 electrons.

questions.stem: Violet light and red light lie at opposite ends of the visible spectrum. How does violet light compare with red light?

options.text: Violet light has the lower frequency, as it has the shorter wavelength.
Violet light has the longer wavelength, as its photons carry more energy.
Violet photons carry less energy, as red is the colour of hot, energetic things.
Violet photons carry more energy, as violet light has the higher frequency.

questions.explanation: Violet light has a shorter wavelength than red, so it has a higher frequency, and photon energy increases with frequency. Violet photons therefore carry more energy than red photons.

questions.stem: Consider the set of lines in the hydrogen emission spectrum produced by electrons falling to n = 2 from higher levels. Which statement about the lines in this set is correct?

options.text: The lines are equally spaced in frequency across the set.
The lines get closer together towards higher frequency.
The lines get closer together towards lower frequency.
The lines are dark gaps across a continuous band of colour.

questions.explanation: The energy levels get closer together as n increases, so the energy differences for falls to n = 2 from n = 3, 4, 5, … increase by ever smaller amounts. The lines therefore converge towards higher frequency.
